Spray a compatible cabinetry coating in thin coats for a smooth finish, then reinstall the doors and drawer fronts. Follow the system’s drying, curing and cleaning guidance before everyday handling.

Peeling films, swelling, moisture damage and structural problems may need repair or replacement before painting is considered. Wood, MDF, laminate and factory finishes need individual assessment for adhesion and coating compatibility.
Is painting or replacing cabinets the better option?

Painting can suit sound cabinets that meet your storage needs. Damaged boxes, failing materials or a layout that no longer works may point toward repairs or replacement. Assess those needs before comparing options.

Clean, prepare and prime the included cabinet surfaces according to the material and selected coating system. Protect surrounding fixtures and agree on component handling.

Should I spray or brush my cabinets?
For cabinet painting, spraying gives the smoothest finish on doors and drawer fronts; brushes suit small touch-ups.
Can you paint thermofoil cabinets?
Firmly attached thermofoil can be painted with a bonding primer. Peeling thermofoil cannot be saved by paint and needs repair or replacement first.
